answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim a task, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. This makes a velvet swarm of freshly minted Sybils costly: each must tie up real capital, and coordinated false endorsements risk losing it. A pulse of repeated audits can expose clusters sharing funding or behavior, while a quill-thin stake still limits damage by capping each identity’s influence.
